page: Microsoft Azure F16-4amds_v7 is a constrained-core virtual machine instance configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at up to 4.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates vector and cryptographic instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance allocates 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding an extensive memory-to-compute ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU.

Local ephemeral storage is provided by a bundled 1890 GB NVMe solid-state drive, enabling rapid read and write access for temporary volumes and swap space alongside Azure Premium Storage compatibility. In benchmark testing, the high-frequency AMD processor delivers top-tier stress-ng single-core CPU throughput of 3772.48 points. Multi-core stress-ng throughput measures at 15055.21 points, matching expectations for a 4-core physical configuration. Small-model language inference (135M) achieves top-tier generation rates at 357.27 tokens per second, while static web serving throughput measures at 10.66 GB per second.

By restricting active compute cores to 4 while retaining 128.0 GB of memory and high-capacity NVMe storage, this instance targets workloads limited by core-based software licensing structures. This design optimizes hardware licensing costs while sustaining large in-memory data structures. Workloads best aligned with this configuration include licensed relational database engines, in-memory key-value stores, memory-bound caching layers, and data transformation jobs that require substantial temporary disk storage.
